findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn’t any hand soap available at either hand sinks along the deli’s cook-line. A bottle of soap was provided to both hand sinks to correct the violation. Ensure that hand soap is available at all hand sinks to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn’t any paper towel available at one of the hand sinks in the deli area. Paper towels were provided to the hand sink to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are provided with paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: There were several packages of cook dinners that lacked proper allergen and ingredient labeling. The dinners were stored in a floor cooler in front of the deli area. Discussed with PIC that all individual dinners will need to list ingredients and allergens. Ensure that packaged food items contain proper allergen and ingredient labeling.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11(B)(5) Food Labels. Major Food Allergen. (B) Label information shall include: (5) The name of the FOOD source for each MAJOR FOOD ALLERGEN contained in the FOOD unless the FOOD source is already part of the common or usual name of the respective ingredient.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: There was a leak observed at the faucet of the triple sink inside of the dish room. Shown and discussed with the person-in-charge. The facility will work to repair the leak. Ensure that the leak is repaired and is in leak-free condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a container of pizza sauce and a container of sausages dated 8/30/2025 in the walk in cooler. Items considered Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food (TCS) are to only be held in house for 7 days and discarded if 7 days are exceeded. PIC discarded items to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS are never held in house for longer than 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the hood system (above the fryers) were observed heavily accumulated with grease debris. Discussed and shown to PIC. The facility has CFB Steam Power for servicing the hood system, however, the baffles are able to be cleaned manually in a ware-washing sink or dish machine. Ensure that hood baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to avoid grease buildup.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The wall behind the wash sink (across from fryers) is in need of re-caulking. The old caulk was observed pulling from the wall. Ensure that gaps are caulked properly to prevent debris buildup in hard to reach places.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed packaged food items such as but not limited pasta salads and trail mixes stored throughout the facility without proper allergen and ingredient labeling. Refer to complaint #25-0118 for further details. The food items were pulled from the shelves. Ensure that packaged food items contain proper allergen and ingredient labeling.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11(B)(5) Food Labels. Major Food Allergen. (B) Label information shall include: (5) The name of the FOOD source for each MAJOR FOOD ALLERGEN contained in the FOOD unless the FOOD source is already part of the common or usual name of the respective ingredient.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Clean dishes were being stored underneath an exposed area where a ceiling tile was missing (in dish room). Discussed and shown to PIC. The missing space was filled with a ceiling tile. Ensure that clean dishes are stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed there to be no hand soap at the handwashing sink to the left of the whole meats display cooler. PIC mentioned that the facility does not have a soap dispenser at that particular sink. There was a bottle of hand sanitizer present. Discussed with PIC that it is required that the handwashing sink has soap available to properly wash hands. Ensure that hand soap is available at all hand-sinks. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
A dented can was observed to be stored on a rack in the backstock area of the deli. Discussed with PIC and the dented can was pulled. Ensure that cans of food are free of dents during storage to prevent contamination. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed to-go containers stored in an upright position on a storage shelf near the main cook line. Discussed with PIC that to-go containers should be stored face down to prevent possible contamination. Ensure to-go containers are always stored in a manner that prevents them from contamination.

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment:
The handwashing sink in the dish room appears to be missing the knee pedal that operates the hot water. There is hot water at the handsink, however, the knee pedal is detached and does not allow hot water to flow freely. PIC used a wrench to show that the facility has hot water at the sink. PIC contacted their plumbing company and was told that the pedal will have to be ordered through the manufacturing company. A follow-up is schedule for 5/6/2024. 

5-103.12: Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, EQUIPMENT, and nonFOOD EQUIPMENT that are required to use water except that water (A) and (B) to a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or in response to a temporary interruption of a water supply need not be under pressure.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The fan grates in the walk-in cooler has an accumulation of dust.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure fan grates are cleaned regularly.

4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of re-caulking:
-Produce sink
-hand sink
Ensure these areas are caulked to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The mop was observed to be stored in the mop sink with the mop head down.  PIC corrected on-site.  Ensure mops are placed in a position to properly air dry after use to prevent mold and mildew accumulation.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the handwashing sink in the dish room. Handwashing sign was provided for management to post.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket at front prep area was observed at 100ppm quat. Fresh solution at 150-200ppm was provided. Ensure sanitizer solutions are changed throughout operations as needed and maintained at 150ppm/above as required by manufacturer’s use instructions. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.
Ens

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Employee in front prep area was observed wiping the stem of a food thermometer with a dry paper towel after use. Use of sanitizer solution to wipe the stem between uses was discussed. A sanitizer solution that was not at proper concentration was used to wipe the food contact surface of the thermometer. Employee was advised to re-wipe the thermometer with fresh solution when sanitizer was replaced. 
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. When using sanitizer to wipe stems between temperature checks, ensure food contact surfaces of thermometers are getting cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Cream cheese stuffed peppers at the olive bar were observed with surface and internal temperatures of 54F and 57F respectively. Olive bar was off and observed at 60F. Manager was unsure as to how long products were out and had an employee discard the cream cheese stuffed peppers. Pickled okra and pickled brussel sprouts have labeling that states “refrigerate after opening” and is not indicated for quality versus safety. Manager was advised to ensure all products are at 41F/below within the next few hours and discard after 4hrs if proper temperature is not reached.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Pot pies and cooked chicken from the previous operating day were observed on a rack in the prep area. Surface temperatures were observed at 70F-71F, and internal temperature of chicken was observed at 60F. Manager was unsure as to how long product was out at room temperature. All foods in question were discarded during inspection. Best practices of keeping foods in the cooler until needed and only getting out what staff are working with in the moment during prep were discussed.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 The handle that allows staff to switch between use of the sprayer and free flowing water at the 3 part sink left faucet was missing. Manager noted a work order has been placed. Pliers are available to switch between free flowing water at the faucet and use of the sprayer until the handle is replaced.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed mold on the raw chicken walk in cooler fans. Fans must be kept clean and free of mold. Mold on fans could contaminate food in the cooler. The cooler fans were cleaned during the inspection to correct the violation.  

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed knives and the knife storage bin to be soiled with old food debris. The manager stated only clean knives are supposed to be stored in the knife storage container. The knives and the container were pulled for cleaning during the inspection. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed multiple soup containers at the salad bar hot holding unit to be 90F. The hot holding unit was not turned up all the way. Soups were discarded. Ensure soups are hot held at 135F or above. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed scoops in sugar and sunflower kernals to have no handle. Scoops were stored inside container. Ensure scoops have handles and the handles are not stored inside the food. Scoops were replaced during inspection.
